name: CA-32
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+14 district held by long-serving incumbent Brad Sherman
Sherman's roughly 50-to-1 fundraising edge; Thompson has under $1,000 on hand
Prediction markets price Sherman near-certain at about 96 percent
No polls or expert ratings suggest the race is competitive
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a heavily Democratic district, an entrenched incumbent, a lopsided money gap, and markets treating the race as settled. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving the outlook away from a comfortable Democratic win.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Sherman or surprise polling showing a single-digit race would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 32nd District leans heavily Democratic, and Brad Sherman has held the seat for decades. He enters the general election with about $2.6 million on hand after raising $2.8 million, while Republican Larry Thompson has raised roughly $53,000 and reported under $1,000 in cash. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Sherman, with little organized opposition on the other side.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the resource gap. Prediction markets put Sherman's chances around 96 percent. The combination of a D+14 electorate, an entrenched incumbent, and a lopsided financial advantage makes an upset unlikely; the realistic question is the size of Sherman's winning margin rather than who prevails in November.
